goals: Mechanistic: quantify the strength of soil-texture control on sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) across the Upper Iowa agricultural landscape by ranking drainage response across texture classes under common forcing
Validation: indirectly check the warm-started water-table / storage regime against sparse in-domain USGS wells; acknowledge no direct drainage-flux validation is possible (tile-drain data missing)
key_processes: vertical water partitioning (ET vs surface runoff vs sub-surface drainage)
unsaturated-zone conductivity / porosity control on recharge and baseflow

model_choice.rationale: Soil texture is a per-column SSURGO lever the single-column ELM can pull directly; low basin relief means climate/elevation is not a competing driver, so a texture-stratified column set isolates the mechanism the question asks about.

answerable: Relative strength / ranking of soil-texture control on sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) under common forcing
Texture control on the full partitioning (ET, surface runoff, drainage) and on water-table/storage state, given a WTD-informed warm start

not_answerable.aspect: Quantitative validation of sub-surface / tile-drainage magnitude against measurements
not_answerable.why: brief lists tile-drain flow data as observations_missing; ELM is also 1-D free-drainage with no tile-drain parameterization, so QDRAI is a drainage analog, not literal tile flow
not_answerable.needs: tile-drain flow observation ingest (and ideally a tile-drainage parameterization)

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by dominant SSURGO texture class, with light replication

classes: silty clay loam / clay loam (poorly-drained lowlands)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: One dominant driver with ~3 contrasting texture classes; 3 replicate columns per class (different landscape positions/forcing cells) separate the texture signal from residual forcing/soil-attribute variation without a blind dense grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Place replicates of each texture class across the basin so each class is sampled in more than one NLDAS cell; concentrate the coarse (sand) and fine (clay loam) end-members that bound the drainage response, and site the fine/poorly-drained class in lowland/valley positions where drainage-vs-runoff contrast is largest.
sampling_strategy.replication: 3 columns per texture class to distinguish texture effect from minor forcing-cell and secondary-soil-property differences.

sampling_plan.group: coarse end-member (sand / loamy sand, outwash terraces)
sampling_plan.reason: High-conductivity upper bound on drainage — expected maximum QDRAI, low surface runoff; anchors the sensitive end of the texture response.
Dominant ag-landscape texture — the central case the basin-wide answer must characterize.

sampling_plan.group: fine end-member (silty clay loam / clay loam, poorly-drained lowlands)
sampling_plan.reason: Low-conductivity lower bound — expected minimum drainage / maximum surface runoff; anchors the opposite end and the tile-drained lowland setting.
Placed on any sparse in-domain USGS well locations to check warm-started water-table state; count is data-dependent (see validation_design), so left at 0 pending well coordinates.

sampling_plan_detail.config_note: Native SSURGO texture per column (the treatment). WTD-informed Fan-2013 warm start required on every column before the analysis window; multi-year window supports both spin-up and a stable drainage climatology. Downstream configurator finalizes exact namelist.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place a validation column at each usable well and compare warm-started/drifted ZWT to observed WTD
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on well density and data availability

validation_design.comparison: none possible in-domain — flagged as a gap; could only be done as an analog at an instrumented tile-drained site elsewhere in the Corn Belt

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: native SSURGO soil texture per column, common NLDAS-2 forcing period, WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.capability: WTD-informed warm start (Fan 2013) and/or multi-year spin-up
requires_capabilities.why: sub-surface drainage/recharge is a slow state; cold start at default 8.8 m water table makes QDRAI an initialization artifact
requires_capabilities.blocks: any meaningful drainage magnitude or ranking

requires_capabilities.capability: gridded SSURGO soil ingest per column
requires_capabilities.why: texture is the treatment axis; each column must carry its native texture class
the natural observable for sub-surface drainage validation in this tile-drained ag basin
requires_capabilities.blocks: direct validation of the drainage flux (currently a gap)

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS well WTD ingest + in-domain well locator
requires_capabilities.why: to place and score the indirect water-table validation columns
ELM QDRAI is free-drainage/baseflow, not engineered tile flow
requires_capabilities.blocks: literal comparison to tile-drain observations even if data existed

assumptions: Basin lies within CONUS NLDAS-2 coverage so all columns get ~12 km location-varying forcing.
At least three contrasting SSURGO texture classes (coarse outwash, silt-loam uplands, fine lowlands) are actually present in the basin.
Low relief (~160 m) means climate/elevation is not a competing driver; forcing is treated as effectively common across the texture treatment.
QDRAI is interpreted as a relative drainage analog, adequate for ranking texture sensitivity.
open_questions: How many USGS wells fall inside HUC 07060002 and have usable water-level records? This sets the validation column count.
Are any instrumented tile-drainage sites (in-domain or regional analog) available to close the drainage-validation gap?
Preferred analysis window within 1980-2018 (e.g. wet vs dry years) — does the user want a drought/wet contrast, or a long-term climatology?
